data.title: Show HN: A “Course” as an MCP Server
data.author: codekarate
data.article_summary:
Mastra 101是一门由Mastra大学的首席产品官Shane Thomas讲解的互动课程，旨在教授如何使用Mastra平台开发和部署AI代理。课程由MCP代理引导，包含三个主要课程，未来将增加更多内容，预计12小时完成。课程全程在代理代码编辑器内进行，代理会逐步指导并协助编写代码，帮助构建具备工具、记忆和MCP功能的实际代理。

课程大纲包括：
1. **构建首个代理**：设置开发环境，构建并部署能从外部来源读取数据、使用自定义工具和记忆之前互动的代理。
2. **添加工具和MCP**：通过MCP服务器连接外部服务，集成电子邮件、社交媒体、GitHub等工具。
3. **添加记忆**：配置代理的记忆功能，使其能够记住对话和用户偏好。

常见问题包括MCP服务器在不同编辑器和系统上的安装问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对一个在线课程的使用体验、技术问题、课程内容以及跨平台适应性的讨论。

不同观点：
• Tokumei-no-hito 提到在MacOS上的浏览器（Brave和Safari）中，课程的“播放介绍”按钮无法正常工作，必须通过JavaScript点击才能继续，且没有明显的“开始课程”选项，只能看到课程大纲和介绍视频，用户体验不佳。
• Gorath 对基于LLM编程的效果感到失望，尤其是在使用windsurf时，LLM无法有效帮助解决实际问题，最终在第二部分因循环连接GitHub的MCP问题而放弃。
• keeganpoppen 对Mastra框架印象深刻，认为它简洁且符合实际工作需求，不像其他一些框架过度设计或功能过于简单。
• hofo 作为新手，关注不同AI平台之间代理（agents）的移植性问题，询问这些概念是否在不同平台上具有可移植性。
• tmaly 对运行一个能与该课程互动的7B模型感兴趣，正在寻找适合的模型来在LM Studio上运行。
• jcmontx 和 Tokumei-no-hito 类似，对如何实际开始课程有疑问，尤其是在Cursor中安装后，如何进入实际操作存在困惑。
• davecyen 对课程持积极态度，认为这是类似于Codecademy的下一代编程学习工具。
• ninkendo 对课程的预期不同，原本期待的是一个能自主完成在线大学课程的LLM系统，并对这种系统的可行性表示好奇。
• justanotheratom 建议制作一个关于如何“参加”课程的视频教程，以帮助其他用户解决使用上的困惑。
• avipeltz 关注课程内容是否涵盖工作流创建，而不仅仅是代理的制作。
• hoppp 提到网站在移动端显示效果不佳，可能需要优化。

补充讨论：
• 技术问题：Tokumei-no-hito 和 jcmontx 对课程开始的操作有疑问，Tokumei-no-hito 还提到了技术解决方案（通过JS点击按钮）。
• 跨平台问题：hofok 关注代理在不同AI平台之间的可移植性，这是一个涉及技术兼容性的问题。
• 用户体验与预期：Gorath 和 ninkendo 对LLM的实际表现与个人预期不符，而 keeganpoppen 和 davecyen 对课程和框架持积极评价。
• 移动端优化问题：hoppp 提到移动端体验不佳，这是技术实现上的一个具体问题。

争议焦点：课程操作的直观性以及LLM在实际编程中的有效性存在争议。部分用户（如Tokumei-no-hito 和 Gorath）遇到技术问题和功能不足，而其他用户（如keeganpoppen 和 davecyen）则持积极态度。

data.title: OpenAI o3-pro
data.author: mfiguiere
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕不同GPT模型版本（如o3-pro、o4-mini等）的性能、实用性和价格的讨论。

不同观点：
• **技术细节与使用体验**：
  ◦ [DanMcInerney] 希望GPT5能在性能上有显著提升，并提到每个新版本在实际任务中表现更好，尽管基准测试显示的改进不大。他建议专门针对任务导向数据进行训练。
  ◦ [eru] 正在测试o3-pro，发现其处理算法问题时速度较慢，且UI经常超时，特别是Android和MacOS应用。
  ◦ [ikerino] 对o3-pro感到失望，认为其输出与常规o3差别不大。

• **模型性能的量化与比较**：
  ◦ [chad1n] 猜测o3-pro可能是最初的o3-preview，而o3可能是其量化版本，并希望有人对模型进行质量对比测试。
  ◦ [manmal] 质疑Pro模型是否仅比基础模型略好，并提出是否人工智能性能提升已接近上限的疑问。

• **价格与性价比**：
  ◦ [mark_l_watson] 不愿升级到Pro账户，尽管负担得起，但怀疑LLM是否是实现其对强大AI梦想的最终路径，并对当前的AI热潮持保留态度。
  ◦ [WhitneyLand] 认为o3已经非常强大，并偏好它超过Anthropic 4和Gemini 2.5，指出高级推理模型在代码生成和编辑中具有显著优势，但成本是需要考虑的因素。

• **其他工具与替代方案**：
  ◦ [honeybadger1] 认为Gemini在速度和准确性上仍然领先。
  ◦ [nickandbadger1] 分享了一个与图像生成相关的示例，转移了话题焦点。

• **价格变动与市场策略**：
  ◦ [ChrisArchitect] 提到OpenAI大幅降低o3价格，并提供相关链接。
  ◦ [tiahura] 讨论了升级到Teams账户和增加o3使用的可能性，并将其与Claude Max的费用进行比较。

补充讨论：
• [paul7986] 抱怨GPT的图像创建功能不足，特别是在生成实用图像时出现错误，强调其在实际应用中的局限性。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在模型的实际性能提升是否显著，以及Pro版本是否物有所值。用户对新版本的期望与实际体验之间存在差距。

总结：讨论围绕模型的性能、价格、实用性及替代方案展开，用户对新版本的性能提升和价格策略持不同看法，部分用户对AI发展持谨慎态度。

data.title: Rohde and Schwarz AMIQ Modulation Generator Teardown
data.author: iamsrp
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者以45美元拍得一台Rohde & Schwarz AMIQ调制发生器的经历，并详细描述了其修复和内部构造。AMIQ是一款双通道任意波形发生器，具有深样本缓冲区，通过两个14位DAC以高达105MHz的采样率输出I/Q信号，常与RF矢量信号发生器（如R&S SMIQ）配合使用，以实现高频调制。该设备无用户界面，需通过外部设备（如运行WinIQSim软件的PC）提供波形数据。文中还探讨了AMIQ的内部架构，包括时钟合成器、DAC、模拟滤波器等，并提到其具备高精度时钟调节和多种输入输出接口选项。尽管AMIQ年代久远，但其性能规格在某些方面仍优于现代软件定义无线电（SDR）设置。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对高端测试设备及其技术细节的讨论

不同观点：
• [aidenn0] 提出将该设备与消费级USB DAC（数字模拟转换器）进行基准测试的兴趣，尤其是关注现代DAC在接近奈奎斯特频率时的动态范围表现。他提到Sound Blaster的动态范围声称高达130dB，但认为实际效果可能因"up to"的营销用语而打折扣。

• [CamperBob2] 对设备中的乘法器设计表示关注，特别提到其基于经典的跨线性核心设计，并补充了相关背景知识，引用了Barrie Gilbert的设计理念。他认为Gilbert是模拟电路领域的杰出人物，建议进一步了解其工作。

• [dusted] 表示对将该设备改装为立体声系统DAC的兴趣，提到自己拥有类似的工业控制设备，并用其进行怀旧游戏，显示出对老旧高端设备的个人使用兴趣。

• [blantonl] 认为这类高端测试设备设计精巧，但只有极少数电气工程师在日常工作中使用，暗示其应用范围较为狭窄且专业。

• [myself248] 对设备内部使用ISA接口与PC主板连接的设计感到意外，认为这种设计合理，因为该部分不需要高数据传输速率且易于接口，显示出对设备内部架构的兴趣。

• [teleforce] 赞赏文章内容，并补充了有关Agilent/Keysight历史背景的信息，提到Silicon Valley的起源与HP（现Keysight）的关系，强调了HP在电子行业中的历史地位。

• [raziel2701] 关注设备拍卖来源问题，指出作者未提及设备拍卖公司的信息，显示出对设备获取渠道的关心。

• [leoh] 以简化解释（ELI5）的形式询问设备用途，表明对设备功能的基本信息需求。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：[aidenn0] 对消费级DAC和高端测试设备之间的性能比较表现出不确定性，特别是对动态范围的实际表现存在疑问，暗示对厂商宣传用语的怀疑。
• 技术细节：[CamperBob2] 对设备中的跨线性电路设计的背景介绍，增加了对设备技术细节的理解难度和深度。
• 历史背景：[teleforce] 补充了有关Silicon Valley起源的历史背景信息，丰富了讨论的广度，将设备与更广泛的科技历史联系起来。
• 实用性：[blantonl] 和 [dusted] 的评论显示出对设备实际应用和个人使用潜力的兴趣，反映出对高端测试设备实用性和可获取性的关注。

Introduction
Every few months, a local company auctions off all kinds of lab, production and test equipment.
I shouldn’t be subscribed to their email list but I am, and that’s one way I end up with more
stuff that I don’t really need.
During a recent auction, I got my hands on a Rohde & Schwarz AMIQ, an I/Q modulation
generator, for a grand total of $45. Add to that another 30% for the auction fee and taxes and
you’re still paying much less than what others would pay for a round of golf? But instead of
one morning of fun, this thing has the potential to keep me busy for many weekends, so what a deal!
(Click to enlarge)
A few days after “winning” the auction, I drove to a dark dungeon of a warehouse in San Jose
to pick up the loot.
The AMIQ has a power on/off button and 3 LEDs and that’s in terms of user interface.
There are no dials, there’s no display. So without any other options, I simply powered it up
and I was immediately greeted by the ominous clicking of a hard drive. I was right:
this thing would keep me entertained for at least a little bit!
(Click to enlarge)
It took a significant amount of effort to restore the machine back to its working state. I’ll
write about that in future blog posts, but let’s start with an overview of the functionality
and a teardown of the R&S AMIQ and then deep dive into some of its analog circuits.
AMIQ prices on eBay vary wildly, from $129 to $2600 at the time of writing this. Even if you
get one of the higher priced ones, you should expect to get a unit that’s close to failing due to
leaking capacitors and a flaky harddrive!
The Rohde & Schwarz AMIQ Modulation Generator
Reduced to an elevator sales pitch, the AMIQ is
a 2-channel arbitrary waveform generator (AWG)
with a deep sample buffer
. That’s it!
It has a streaming buffer that feeds samples to 2 14-bit DACs at a sample rate of up to 105MHz.
Two output channels I and Q will typically contain quadrature modulation signals that are sent
to an RF vector signal generator such as a Rohde & Schwarz SMIQ for the actual high-frequency
modulation. In a typical setup, the AMIQ is used to generate the baseband modulated signal and
the SMIQ shifts the baseband signal to an RF frequency.
Since the AMIQ has no user interface, the waveform data must provided by an external
device. This could be a PC that runs R&S WinIQSim software or even the SMIQ itself because it has
the ability to control an AMIQ. You can also create your own waveforms and upload them via floppy disk,
GPIB or an RS-232 interface using
SCPI control commands
.
Figure 4-1 of the
AMIQ Operating Manual
has a
simplified block diagram. It is pretty straightforward and somewhat similar to the one of my
HP 33120A function generator
:
(Click to enlarge)
On the left are 2 blocks that are shared:
a clock synthesizer
waveform memory
And then for each channel:
14-bit D/A converter
analog filters
output section with amplifier/attenuator
differential analog output driver (AMIQ-B2 option)
The major blocks are surrounded by a large amount of DACs that are used to control everything from
the tuning input of local 10MHz clock oscillator, gain and offset of output signals, clock skew
between I and Q signal and much more.
You could do some of this with a modern SDR setup, but the specifications of the AMIQ units
are dialed up a notch. Both channels are completely symmetrical to avoid modulation errors at the
source. If there’s a need to compensate for small delay differences in, for example, the external
cables, you can compensate for that by changing the skew between clocks of the output DACs with a
precision of 10ps. Similarly, the DAC sample frequency can be programmed with 32-bit precision.
(Click to enlarge)
In addition to the main I/Q outputs at the front, there are a bunch of secondary input and output signals:
10MHz reference input and output
sample clock
trigger input
marker output
external filter loopback output and input
bit error rate measurement (BER) connector (AMIQ-B1 option)
parallel interface with the digital value of the samples that are sent to the DAC (front panel, AMIQ-B3 option)
(Click to enlarge)
Above those speciality inputs and outputs are the obligatory GPIB interface and a bunch of generic connectors
that look suspiciously like the ones you’d find on an early century PC:
PS/2 keyboard and mouse
Parallel port
RS232
USB
There are 3 different AMIQ versions:
1110.2003.02: 4M samples
1110.2003.03: 4M samples
1110.2003.04: 16M samples
Mine is an AMIQ-04.
WinIQSim Software
While it is possible to control the AMIQ over RS-232 or GPIB with your own software, you’d have
a hard time matching

data.author: prismatic
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了秘鲁艺术家Elena Izcue于1926年在巴黎出版的《El arte peruano en la escuela》系列绘本，该书通过从原住民陶瓷和纺织品中提取图案，旨在让小学生了解并自豪于本土艺术传统。当时，秘鲁艺术界正围绕是否应将印加艺术纳入教育展开争论，而Izcue的作品呼应了印第安美学运动，试图从 pre-Columbian 传统中寻找国家艺术的未来。她的绘本不仅用于课堂，还推动了本土手工艺复兴，影响了巴黎和美国的时尚设计界。Izcue的创作被视为秘鲁艺术复兴的重要推动力，尽管她在国际上获得认可，但其贡献常未被明确提及。

Drawing on Tradition: Elena Izcue’s
Peruvian Art in the School
(1926)
Elena Izcue,
El arte peruano en la escuela
, vol. 1 (Paris: Editorial Excelsior, 1926).
The 1930 course catalogue at Lima’s Escuela Nacional de Bellas Artes (National School of Fine Arts) announced a new class that would spark months of fierce debate in the popular press. In an
open letter
published in the newspaper
El Comercio
, Antonino Espinosa Saldaña heavily criticized the school’s inclusion of a lecture series on Inca art, stating quite bluntly that such a thing did not exist. “It was not a civilization of aesthetes, cultivators of beauty, of line, of color, of form”, the painter wrote, and while Espinosa deemed the output of earlier cultures in the region more striking, applying even these motifs to contemporary works would produce only “annoying agglomerations of incomprehensible monsters”. The ENBA’s Inca art class — and the calumny it provoked — took place against the backdrop of the ascendent Indigenist aesthetic movement, which sought to anchor Peru’s artistic future in the pre-Columbian past, skipping over, as it did so, the gilt-bedecked products of Spanish colonial rule. Debates about something as innocuous as an art class, then, were shorthand for much larger and more fundamental questions about the nature of Peruvian national identity in the modern era and the position of Indigenous people in society.
It was in the context of these aesthetic and political currents that the designer Elena Izcue produced
El arte peruano en la escuela
(Peruvian art in the school), a set of drawing workbooks featuring motifs taken from Indigenous ceramics and textiles. Published by Editorial Excelsior in Paris in 1926 (although some date the second volume later, to 1929), the two books feature lizards, llamas, and pelicans capering over gridded pages, which both facilitate copywork and highlight the geometric sophistication of each design. (A third volume, referenced by archival sources, appears to have been scrapped due to budgetary constraints.) Izcue’s books came amid a wave of excavations across Peru that radically altered our understanding of the pre-Hispanic world. Julio C. Tello, the godfather of Peruvian archaeology and an acquaintance of Izcue, had recently published his findings on Chavín de Huántar, one of the oldest known urban centers in the Americas. Around the time
El arte peruano
went to print, he also unearthed hundreds of magnificent Paracas textiles at a coastal necropolis with the help of his student Toribio Mejía Xesspe, who would shortly go on to provide the first scholarly description of the Nazca Lines, monumental millennia-old geoglyphs in the desert of southern Peru.
Izcue was deeply influenced by the ancient history that was being rewritten around her, and she wanted to make sure that young people felt pride in autochthonous artistic achievements that had long been either ignored or openly disparaged. “For the first time”, the preface crows, “an effort has been made to extract from the buried traditions of the past — literally buried in cemeteries — the elements of a renaissance of popular art”.
Elena Izcue,
El arte peruano en la escuela
, vol. 2 (Paris: Editorial Excelsior, 1926).
Though Izcue largely frames
El arte peruano
as classroom material for primary school students, contemporary commentators
emphasized
another equally important use for the books: revitalizing domestic craft production by grafting it to a non-European fount of influence. The second volume provides suggestions for what kinds of objects — from book covers to curtains — might be most suited to each motif and even includes visual aids for how the figures might be flipped and tessellated. The adaptation of a pre-Hispanic visual vocabulary to modern design work would become a calling card for Izcue over the course of her own career: after winning a government scholarship in 1927, she moved to Paris along with her sister Victoria (an artist in her own right) and began studying under Fernand Léger. Izcue’s Indigenist aesthetic was
enthusiastically received
by the Parisian fashion world, and she soon found work with couturiers such as House of Worth and Elsa Schiaparelli, who attributes the inspiration for her signature “shocking pink” in part to Andean weaving (though it is worth noting that her employers rarely acknowledged Izcue’s contributions explicitly). Reviews of a 1935 art exhibition that Izcue curated in New York say that Peruvian-inspired designs had become all the rage in the United States, while another credits Izcue with setting off an artistic renaissance in Peru akin to Diego Rivera in Mexico.

data.author: akchro
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者因无法负担Apple Vision Pro的高昂价格，决定自制类似功能的眼动追踪网页项目——Eyesite。作者使用WebGazer.js库进行眼动校准，通过让用户注视屏幕不同位置来实现精准的眼动追踪，并用其替代鼠标操作。为了提升体验，作者去除了显示眼动位置的红色光标，使用户感觉更自然。当用户注视按钮时，按钮会有发光和弹出效果作为反馈。由于眼动追踪不够精准，作者增大了UI尺寸以提高可用性。该项目代码可在GitHub上查看，是一个有趣且具创意的实验性项目。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：眼动追踪技术在用户体验（UX）中的应用与改进

不同观点：
• **weeb**：提出两个改进眼动追踪UX的建议：
  1. **校准过程无聊**：建议改进校准过程的用户体验，比如通过让用户盯着点使它们晃动和消失，像Tobii的游戏化校准一样，让过程更有趣。
  2. **眼动反馈不准确**：强调眼动反馈的重要性，提到Tobii的"ghost overlay"方法，可以在校准后提供近似反馈，帮助用户调整误差。

• **jll29**：引用了学术研究，提供了与眼动追踪相关的几篇重要论文，如WebGazer软件的介绍和几篇关于使用眼动数据改进用户体验的研究文章，强调了该领域的学术背景和已有研究。

• **BugsJustFindMe**：对应用要求最小屏幕尺寸提出质疑，质疑其必要性，表明对技术要求的不解或不满。

• **naveen_k**：分享了自己正在进行的一个类似项目，使用眼动追踪和Mediapipe的面部标志模型进行光标预测实验，对文中提到的校准方法表示认同，并计划继续优化自己的项目。

• **cwmoore**：表达了对眼动追踪技术潜在隐私问题的担忧，认为只要有摄像头，眼动追踪和情感预测就可能存在，甚至可能被广泛使用。

• **mdrzn**：认为当前的眼动追踪技术仍不够成熟（晃动且需要大的UI），但期待未来能够通过眼动完成阅读和导航等任务，认为这是非常自然的交互方式。

• **renierbotha**：建议开发一款使用眼动追踪进行瞄准等操作的WebGL游戏，认为这将是非常酷且具有可访问性的游戏，扩展了眼动追踪的应用场景。

• **holografix**：表示对实验性人机交互（HCI）项目的热爱，认为这样的项目能启发其对计算机和技术的不同思考，强调了技术创新的激励作用。

• **estsauver**：简单直接地表达了对该眼动追踪演示的喜爱，认为这是非常酷且有趣的演示，给予了积极的反馈。

补充讨论：
- **争议焦点**：目前没有明显的争议，但**BugsJustFindMe**对技术要求提出质疑，表明对某些技术限制的不解。
- **重要论据**：
  1. **weeb**提出的游戏化校准和眼动反馈建议，提供了具体的例子（Tobii的游戏化校准）。
  2. **jll29**提供的学术论文支持，展示了该领域的已有研究成果。
  3. **cwmoore**对隐私问题的担忧，提出了技术可能带来的社会问题。

整体来看，讨论围绕眼动追踪技术的改进、应用场景和潜在问题展开，参与者分享了各自的观点和项目经验，提供了有价值的建议和反馈。

I wanted Apple Vision Pros, but I don’t have $3,500 in my back pocket. So I made Apple Vision Pros at home.
I was interested in making a project that combined computer vision with web design—a website that users could
physically
interact with. This inspired me to make
Eyesite
, because who needs a mouse when you have your eyes?
Eye tracking
Luckily, there is already a Javascript library for eye tracking called
WebGazer.js
. We can achieve decent eye tracking through calibration:
Make the user look at a point and click. This maps the current gaze to a point on the screen.
Feed the gaze/coordinate mapping into WebGazer to calibrate.
Repeat 9x times on the corners, sides, and center to get good mapping data.
I found that it was best to get 5 mappings per point for better eye tracking accuracy.
Calibration in debug mode. The top right shows how WebGazer tracks your eyes and face. The red dot is where it thinks I’m looking.
Website Interaction
Now that we have eye tracking, we can make some cool things with it! I decided to use the user’s gaze as a mouse and have them click with spacebar—kind of like how Apple Vision Pros have you look and pinch. Although I had the main functionality, it was far from finished. There were many considerations with making the experience as smooth and immersive as possible.
The “Invisible” Mouse
Initially, the user could see “where” they were looking at through a red dot.
Main page in debug mode.
This created some problems. First, the red dot was distracting, and users would unconsciously look at it instead of my buttons. Second, the red dot revealed how inaccurate the eye tracking was, which ruined the immersion.
Ultimately, I decided to remove the “eye cursor” and also make the user’s mouse invisible. It made you really feel like you were controlling the website with your eyes rather than moving a mouse around. You can turn on debug mode to see your eye cursor and mouse.
User feedback
Since we don’t have a mouse, we need some way for the user to know they are looking at something. To do this… we track the user’s gaze (how surprising). We hid the eye cursor, but we still have the x and y coordinates of the user’s gaze. Each button component has checks to see if that gaze is within its borders. When the component detects the user is looking at it, it responds with a slight glow and pop.
Large UI
Admittedly, the eye tracking is not the best. You can really see how jittery it is with debug mode on. So I decided to make the UI huge. I also added a screen size restriction so the site is only usable on displays that meet a minimum size threshold (Sorry mobile users! It wouldn’t work on your phone anyway).
The large size of the button accounts for the jitteriness of the eye tracking.
Conclusion
Those were a few details about Eyesite. If you are interested, you can see the source code. Small warning: this project was just a small demo and isn’t a shining example of clean code or best practices.
This was a really fun project to make, and super cool to use too. If you want to make your own computer vision project or improve this one, I encourage you to do so! You can find the project at
https://github.com/akchro/eyesite
.
44253307.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者因无法负担Apple Vision Pro的高昂价格，决定自制类似功能的眼动追踪网页项目——Eyesite。作者使用WebGazer.js库进行眼动校准，通过让用户注视屏幕不同位置来实现精准的眼动追踪，并用其替代鼠标操作。为了提升体验，作者去除了显示眼动位置的红色光标，使用户感觉更自然。当用户注视按钮时，按钮会有发光和弹出效果作为反馈。由于眼动追踪不够精准，作者增大了UI尺寸以提高可用性。该项目代码可在GitHub上查看，是一个有趣且具创意的实验性项目。

整体来看，讨论围绕眼动追踪技术的改进、应用场景和潜在问题展开，参与者分享了各自的观点和项目经验，提供了有价值的建议和反馈。

data.title: My Cord-Cutting Adventure (2020)
data.author: wizardforhire
data.article_summary: 本文作者讲述了自己作为消费者在“剪线”（放弃传统有线电视服务）过程中的经历与挫折。过去，消费者可以轻松购买各种录像设备，如VCR、DVR等，但如今这类设备在市场上几乎消失，尤其是在加拿大。电视服务提供商如Shaw、Rogers、Bell等通过限制录像功能来维护自身利益，导致消费者无法方便地录制和保存电视内容。作者的DVR设备不仅存在技术问题，还受到服务商的严格控制，如专有格式使得内容只能在特定设备上播放，且设备维修和使用也受限。最终，作者对这种缺乏选择和自由的市场现状感到失望，认为这是对消费者权益的剥夺。

主要讨论点： cord-cutting（切断有线电视）的方法、技术工具的推荐与使用体验

不同观点：

• thom怀念TiVo的产品设计和用户体验，认为尽管现代流媒体选择更多，但TiVo的体验更令人满意。
• javier_e06使用HD天线和Roku在旅行时观看直播电视，并对某些体育赛事被有线电视垄断表示不满。
• don-code详细描述了自己复杂的家庭电视系统设置，包括Kubernetes集群和自建DVR功能，认为这种设置优于传统方案。
• robbiet480支持Channels DVR，强调其跨平台支持和API集成的优点。
• BeetleB推荐Plex TV Guide，认为这是简单易行的解决方案，但对Android应用的改版表示不满。
• badc0ffee的Shaw DVR在取消电视订阅后仍然可用，但对录制时间不匹配的问题感到困扰。
• bdcravens尝试过使用天线和Fire TV Recast进行DVR，效果尚可，但提到使用封闭解决方案的常见问题。
• x187463对整个讨论表示质疑，认为这些努力只是为了观看广告，不值得。
• jbm查看了tvfool并发现当地可用频道很少，认为租蓝光碟片是更省心的选择。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是cord-cutting的难易程度，有些人认为现代技术让这个过程变得简单，而另一些人则认为对普通用户来说仍然复杂。
• 另一个讨论点是不同工具和服务的优劣，如HDHomerun、Channels DVR、Plex和TiVo等，用户根据自己的经验和需求有不同偏好。
• 对加拿大电视频道的失望和对商业化体育转播的不满也是讨论的重要部分，反映了用户对内容可获得性的关注。
• 技术设置的复杂性也是一个重要话题，从简单的AppleTV到复杂的Kubernetes集群，不同用户有不同的技术能力和需求。

44220890.article_content:
My Cord-Cutting Adventure
I'm not into conspiracy theories, but you'd swear there was one against cord-cutting.  Cord-cutting shouldn't be any more of an "adventure" than buying a toaster. But it is.
For starters, the consumer electronics industry, normally so eager to sell us computers, laptops, pads, phones, and watches; the industry that for 30 years has sold us VCRs, competed over Beta vs VHS and Super-VHS (look it up, it existed), then sold us DVDs, DVD recorders with DVD-R and DVD-RW, then sold us DVRs that recorded standard definition, then sold us Blu-Ray players of increasing degrees of quality and declining prices...these days, they've utterly given up selling us anything that can record video.
The DVR was so beloved, the culmination of decades of home video-entertainment recording into the most-convenient possible form, it was called "God's Machine" by the chair of the FCC.
Casus Belli
Now they are gone from stores, at least in Canada. The change shows us how little oligopoly differs from monopoly where it counts.   Canada has a very tight little oligopoly of TV providers: Shaw, Rogers, Bell, Telus - few enough to meet in an apartment bathroom.   There was no objective, technical reason to extend this oligopoly from TV signals to the consumer electronics of video recorders.  Great technical agonies had been already done to ensure that the new HDTV video plug, "HDMI", would be required to include "HDCP" - high-def copy protection - so that you couldn't just take a video signal from your Blu-Ray and make another Blu-Ray.  The same could have been applied to cable movies.
Even participating in that restriction of user rights to copy was already a new legal innovation.  The cable/satellite companies had no stake of their own in whether Disney movies could be copied and the purchase of discs avoided. One would think they'd be compelled to help Disney's bottom line only at gunpoint, their own interests being to give their customers the best TV experience they could.  People had been recording TV for 20 years when the HDTV switch came along; the function was a very free and open market, as many firms competed to come up with the best recorder features, quality and price - and that free market worked its magic, the products kept getting better.  Shutting down that free market, into a literal company store of bad choices, was not in consumer's interest.
Content providers had already been proven wrong when they freaked out at this, industry spokesman Jack Valenti comparing the VCR to the Boston Strangler.  Instead, people loved to buy commercial tapes and discs as presents, the ownership of a TV-recorded movie having all the cachet that "music recorded from radio" had enjoyed since the cassette tape came out in 1969: none.
But their paranoia broke out again with digital recording: it would be of perfect quality, eliminate the stigma, and wipe out their disc sales.   Oddly, at the time, the ability to do perfect digital music copies from CD to CD-R was not really destroying the music industry.   All the destruction was happening from low-quality MP3 recordings being
very easily available
by download.
Since then, movie disc sales have been drastically reduced by the comparable easy availability of video streaming.  Even worse for disc rentals: the convenience of Netflix actually killed video stores, just as they jumped to high-quality Blu-Rays. The lower quality of streaming had nothing to do with it.
It doesn't really require a conspiracy theory where Disney and Universal conspire with cable-TV to kill off home recording; if the cablecos could make money by doing it, they'd need no other incentive.
I rented or purchased, from both Shaw Cable and Bell Satellite, two different DVR machines over the early 21st century.  They were pretty good quality compared to the standard-def DVR I'd used in the late 1990s that could burn its hard-drive recordings to DVD-R.  They were still trying to sell the new, more-expensive, HDTV at all, with many not seeing much from it.
With the Shaw HD-DVR, however, there was no way to save content. Indeed, while the Shaw effort could save even more movies to a plug-in hard drive, all your content was lost if you stopped your cable subscription: the recording format was (pointlessly) proprietary, and only your rented Shaw DVR could read it.  You could "buy" the DVR with time-payments, which meant that any repairs could still only be done by Shaw, who would charge you for repairing your property - but you still couldn't use it without the subscription running.
The Final Straw
Then in 2015, I moved, and we got the new, CRTC-demanded, minimal cable subscription for $25 per month; and paid more to rent/buy a minimal DVR.   Minimal was the word for it.  The computer that runs it is so inadequate to the task that it frequently reboots, often while recording, leaving a truncated recording.  The lack of CPU horsepower is revealed by its response to a series of commands from the remote: more

data.title: The Seymour Cray Era of Supercomputers
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary: 《西摩·克雷时代的超级计算机》回顾了西摩·克雷主导超级计算机发展的三十年间技术和商业历史。书中详细介绍了主要超级计算机型号的发展、技术决策和市场变化，特别聚焦于克雷的公司及其竞争者如IBM、Control Data Corporation、Texas Instruments和Fujitsu。早期计算机分为“商业计算”和“科学计算”两大类，克雷的CDC 6600以其卓越性能闻名，而IBM 360则主导了商业市场。书中讨论了各行业的“关键问题”以及超级计算机如何从政府和大学扩展到工业领域。随着市场变化，超级计算机技术向大规模并行处理转变，软件支持和操作系统开发也逐渐成为重点。本书适合对科学计算历史、计算机架构及高价值/低产量商业策略感兴趣的读者。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Cray超级计算机的历史、技术性能及其现代对比的讨论

不同观点：
• [mark-r] 分享了其参观Cray工厂的个人经历，强调了Cray团队对冷却系统的自豪感以及与Cray本人见面的细节，还提到一个与Cray-3相关的轶事。
• [chasil] 讨论了Cray-1和CDC 6600的技术架构，包括其处理器设计、时钟频率以及与现代处理器（如RISC-V和ARM）的比较，突出了其历史和技术演变。
• [mattgrice] 指出文章封面上的Cray 3是唯一一台从未出售的机器，提醒读者注意这一细节。
• [glimshe] 推荐了一个技术博物馆，指出该博物馆展示了许多超级计算机，包括Cray系列，为对超级计算机感兴趣的人提供了实际参观的建议。
• [watersb] 讨论了现代微控制器与Cray-1性能的对比，提到了具体 benchmark 测试（如Gibson Mix和Livermore Loops），并指出某些现代设备（如Raspberry Pi 4和ARM Cortex-M4+）在浮点运算性能上已经远超Cray-1。

补充讨论：
• [dvh] 以幽默的方式质疑超级计算机是否需要配备家具，反映了一些人对超级计算机形象的刻板印象。
• [ferguess_k] 表达了对Cray及其超级计算机的浓厚兴趣，计划深入阅读相关书籍。
• [webprofusion] 对文章缺乏图片表示失望，表明其对视觉内容的期待。

争议焦点：

总体而言，评论涵盖了Cray超级计算机的历史背景、技术细节及其现代技术对比，同时包含了一些个人经历和博物馆推荐等实用信息。

44252858.article_content:
The Seymour Cray Era of Supercomputers (Review)
2025-06-11
The Seymour Cray Era of Supercomputers: From Fast Machines to Fast Codes
is a technical and business history of the roughly three-decades when Seymour Cray dominated the development of a class of computer called the “supercomputer”. The book covers the development of the major supercomputer models, the technical decisions and trade-offs involved, and changes to the market. The book ends with SGI’s purchase of Cray’s assets and the transition to massively parallel processing.
The Seymour Cray Era of Supercomputers: From Fast Machines to Fast Codes
. By Boelie Elzen and Donald MacKenzie. ACM Books. ISBN 979-8-4007-1369-9.
DOI
10.1145/3705551
.
Early on, computer designs were bifurcated between the domains of “business computing” and “scientific computing.” Business computing was almost exclusively fixed-point, dealt with categorical and string data, often I/O bound, and had a broad base of less technical users with often similar problems (e.g. payroll). Scientific computing heavily used floating point, dealt with complex numerical data such as matrices and chains of differential equations, often CPU bound, and featured a very small base of highly
technical users with specialized and often unique problems (e.g. national laboratories).
In 1964, this bifurcation was exemplified by the release of two products. IBM launched the IBM 360, a new computing platform that came to dominate business management. Control Data Corporation (CDC), co-founded by Seymour Cray, released the CDC 6600. While IBM sold more than 1,000 in its first month, the CDC took a decade to sell 100. However, the 6600 claimed the moniker “fastest computer in the world” and only relinquished the claim to its successor, the 6700. Although IBM could take solace in finding greater monetary success in a much larger market, Thomas J. Watson Jr. was mortified that IBM had lost the performance crown to a tiny team with far fewer resources.
Over ten chapters, the authors chronicle the technical developments that kept supercomputers at the performance edge for the next three decades. The book covers the development of the CRAY-1 and the other major models that came out of Cray’s companies, as well as CDC, IBM, Texas Instruments, and Fujitsu efforts to compete in the area. Supercomputers expanded from a small pool of government and university customers into industries such as aerospace, petroleum, and automotive and the authors discuss each industry’s “hero problems” and the computer vendors approached the new markets. The book ends as economics shift and massively parallel processing becomes the dominant approach.
Technology development is inherently risky and the book goes into detail on the many false starts and near misses. Although the focus of the book is usually on hardware and physical concerns such as wire propagation delay, the book pays attention to software concerns in parallel to market changes. Early on, supercomputer customers wrote almost all of their own software but, as the market grew, customers expected more software support from vendors. The latter half of the book includes discussion of operating system development, evolution of compilers (mostly Fortran) and their interplay with instruction sets, and specialized tools for specific industries (e.g. computational fluid dynamics). I was unaware of the early resistance to Unix and the concern that it was “slow.”
As a criticism, the text ignores aesthetics and personalities of the people involved. We learn very little about Seymour Cray or any other designer’s personality or what it was like to work for them. Yet, supercomputers were deliberately designed to beautiful or at least evocative. This sterility of the text and its approach misses an important aspect of why people were drawn to supercomputers and their impact in the culture.
The book is available digitally, in paperback, and hardbound. I read the paperback version which is printed on demand. The text and photos were crisp and highly readable, although the ink did bleed through the pages. Additionally, the left-hand internal margin was tighter than comfortable, although not so tight as to obscure any of the text.
Recommended for this interested in the history of scientific computing, computer architecture, and high-value/low-volume business strategy.
44252858.article_summary: 《西摩·克雷时代的超级计算机》回顾了西摩·克雷主导超级计算机发展的三十年间技术和商业历史。书中详细介绍了主要超级计算机型号的发展、技术决策和市场变化，特别聚焦于克雷的公司及其竞争者如IBM、Control Data Corporation、Texas Instruments和Fujitsu。早期计算机分为“商业计算”和“科学计算”两大类，克雷的CDC 6600以其卓越性能闻名，而IBM 360则主导了商业市场。书中讨论了各行业的“关键问题”以及超级计算机如何从政府和大学扩展到工业领域。随着市场变化，超级计算机技术向大规模并行处理转变，软件支持和操作系统开发也逐渐成为重点。本书适合对科学计算历史、计算机架构及高价值/低产量商业策略感兴趣的读者。

data.title: Bliss – The story behind one of the most famous photographs (2012)
data.author: susam
data.article_summary: 《我是马丁·帕尔》（I Am Martin Parr）是一部由李·舒尔曼（Lee Shulman）执导的 intimate 纪录片，深入探讨了英国著名摄影师马丁·帕尔的生活与作品。影片通过展示帕尔的摄影历程和个人经历，揭示了他对社会、文化和日常生活的独特视角。文章作者彼得·登奇（Peter Dench）参加了该片在伦敦的首映，并对影片及帕尔的艺术成就进行了进一步了解。影片为观众呈现了一个既有深度又富有人情味的摄影大师形象。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对某张图片的评价及其文化影响

不同观点：
• [metalman的观点] 认为该图片没有给人留下深刻印象，属于不对称影响（asymmetric influence）的例子。他指出该图片并不著名，也没有引起人们的注意，甚至将其描述为“ubiquitous grot”（无处不在的糟粕）。Metalman个人没有认出这张图片，除非有注释说明，并认为所有被强加的“选项”都是试图将一切制度化的证据。他质疑是否真的有粉丝基础存在，并暗示这种现象是试图将一切纳入制度化的一部分。

• [esafak的观点] 认为该图片看起来不真实，因为其色彩过于饱和且曝光过度，特别是云层部分。他不认为这是一张好照片，因为没有任何细节能吸引人的注意力，尤其不能理解它为何能作为Windows桌面背景图片使用多年。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点在于该图片为何能广泛传播并长期使用，尽管两位评论者都对图片的质量和影响力持怀疑态度。
- Metalman提到了图片被制度化和强加于用户的观点，暗示了对这种文化现象的批评。
- Esafak则从技术角度（如饱和度和曝光）对图片质量进行了评价，认为其缺乏吸引力。
- 两者都对该图片作为长期桌面背景的选择表示不理解，但各自的论据不同：一个是从文化和制度角度，另一个是从技术和美学角度。

data.title: Unveiling the EndBOX – A microcomputer prototype for EndBASIC
data.author: jmmv
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一款名为EndBOX的怀旧计算机，其设计目标是重现过去简单直接的编程体验。EndBOX启动后直接进入EndBASIC环境，专为喜欢探索和学习编程的“黑客”及教育工作者设计，尤其适合那些怀念老式计算机的人。设备配有小屏幕而非键盘，用户可自由选择输入设备如键盘、手柄等。目前有两款原型：标准型配备7英寸触屏，基于Raspberry Pi 3B+；微型版则使用128x128 LCD，基于Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W。EndBOX运行定制的EndBOX OS，基于NetBSD，支持USB和Wi-Fi，且具抗断电特性。文章呼吁读者支持这一项目，帮助其实现批量生产。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Raspberry Pico上的PicoMite作为编程平台的优缺点，以及与其他类似平台的比较。

不同观点：
• [DrNosferatu] 推荐PicoMite作为Raspberry Pico上的简化替代方案，提供了一个专门的网页链接，介绍PicoMite的功能和使用。
• [zokier] 对视频中展示的10秒启动时间表示遗憾，认为与即时进入代码的时代相比，这是一个退步。虽然承认这可能只是个人偏好，且10秒并不是最差的启动时间，但仍对Raspberry Pi和NetBSD的优化程度提出质疑。
• [abraxas] 将PicoMite与Maximite系列硬件及其Basic克隆进行比较，认为快速Basic在专用硬件上是教授编程的绝佳方式，并希望这种设置能够进入学校系统，成为像BBC Micro在英国那样的标准教学平台。
• [nopakos] 对PicoMite的界面表示赞赏，认为其颜色、字体和提示符让人想起Amstrad CPC，带有一种怀旧情感。
• [dshacker] 对如何编写WIFI驱动程序表示好奇，特别是如何用BASIC创建WIFI驱动程序，并对实现细节提出疑问。
• [_sbrk] 提供了一个关于CH32V003微控制器的链接，暗示这是一个更便宜的选择，但没有详细说明。
• [90s_dev] 认为PicoMite不错，但质疑为何不选择像Pick 9那样的GUI开发环境，暗示GUI可能更适合某些开发者。

补充讨论：
• 启动时间是其中一个争议点，特别是对即时启动有期待的用户群体。
• PicoMite与Maximite的比较及其在教育领域的潜力也是一个讨论重点，尤其是作为教学工具的价值。
• 对如何实现WIFI驱动程序的技术细节有进一步的探讨需求，显示出社区对技术实现的兴趣。
• 对不同开发环境的选择和偏好反映出用户在使用体验和功能需求上的多样性。

44253065.article_content:
Published on: June 6, 2025
Remember when turning a computer on meant instantly jumping into code? No bloat, no distractions—just you and a prompt? That’s the experience I’ve been working to bring back with the EndBOX: a small, resilient, nostalgia-packed, all-screen computer that boots straight into the retro-inspired EndBASIC environment you already know.
And today, six months after its inception, I’m excited to formally show you the first working prototypes—though they are still rough and need refinement. Let’s dive into the goals for the EndBOX and what it could become with your help.
💾 Sponsor the EndBOX
Who is the EndBOX for?
First and foremost, the EndBOX is for the hacker types: those of you who love tinkering with systems, languages, and hardware. But more specifically, the EndBOX caters to those who grew up with simpler computers and know that, to truly understand the fundamentals of computing, you have to experience them from the ground up with as few layers of abstraction as possible.
That said, EndBASIC has always been about providing a learning tool for coding. That was my original goal when I set out to create this language, and that goal is still very much alive. So… the EndBOX can also cater to educators as an all-in-one platform to teach kids how to program through a toy that feels personal.
What makes the EndBOX special?
The EndBOX is intended to be a small, portable device that bundles:
an embedded computer board,
a tablet-sized screen, and
a slim OS that boots straight into EndBASIC.
Why a screen and not a keyboard though? After all, old BASIC machines from the 1980s bundled the computer into the keyboard and let you supply the TV—I mean monitor. Personally, I feel this is not the best form factor in this day and age of touch screens. I want the device to feel playful. And I want to give you the freedom to connect different input peripherals as you see fit.
Put another way: the EndBOX aims to offer a standalone device that can run EndBASIC programs—and how you interact with them, be it via a keyboard, a mouse, a touch screen, a game pad, or even GPIO-attached inputs… should be up to you. In fact, some programs may not need input at all!
Concept of the EndBOX with two SNES-like USB gamepads. EndBASIC does not yet support gamepad input, but it will.
What hardware will the EndBOX have?
Right now, I have built two different EndBOX prototypes:
The standard model
, which sports a 7" HDMI touch display, USB ports, and a GPIO port (which is usable from EndBASIC but not easily accessible in this build). The current prototype is based on the
Raspberry Pi 3B+
, but future builds will likely use a smaller board for a thinner profile.
The prototype of the EndBOX I.
The micro model
, which sports a tiny 128x128 LCD and a micro USB port. The current prototype is based on the
Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W
.
The prototype of the EndBOX I Micro.
Both models provide Wi-Fi to access the EndBASIC cloud file sharing service and should (eventually) also support Bluetooth for peripheral connectivity.
What OS will the EndBOX run?
The EndBOX will run, for lack of a better name, the EndBOX OS. This OS is a quick-to-boot disk image, built on
NetBSD
, that just exposes EndBASIC. The primary goal behind the OS is get you to a prompt as quickly as possible while offering “advanced” features like USB input and Wi-Fi connectivity. A secondary goal is to be resilient to power cuts: you should be able to yank power and reboot the machine at any time to get back to a known-good state, just like you used to do.
The EndBASIC shell is a fork of EndBASIC that integrates with
NetBSD’s console framebuffer
and
other hardware interfaces
, and that provides a mechanism to control the machine from within the EndBASIC interpreter. In particular, the system exposes a
CONFIG.BAS
configuration file—inspired by MS-DOS’s
CONFIG.SYS
—to tune the behavior of the machine (such that you can, for example, modify the font used by the console or configure Wi-Fi networks).
The default configuration file with an override for the
console
setting to select a yellow-on-blue console and a larger font.
Want to help? Here’s how!
While I have a prototype in my hands, I cannot provide one to you just yet. Distributing electronics is a tricky business, and to do it correctly I need to make a plan and deal with various legalities. Plus, depending on scale, I’ll have to figure out production since, for now, I only know
how to build
a limited number of units.
So what I’m wondering today is whether YOU feel this is worth pursuing at all. The EndBOX isn’t just a computer—it’s a philosophy. It’s about computing that’s transparent, approachable, and fun. It’s about helping the next generation fall in love with programming the way we did: by typing on a real machine, with no distractions, and watching code come alive instantly.
Sounds crazy? Yes, it sure does! And
that’s why I need your support

data.title: The curious case of shell commands, or how "this bug is required by POSIX" (2021)
data.author: wonger_
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了在Linux和UNIX系统中使用诸如`bash`、`ssh`、`i3`、`screen`、`tmux`、`dtach`等工具时，它们通常依赖`system(3)`函数通过`sh -c`执行命令，而不是直接调用`execve(2)`。这种设计可能导致安全问题，特别是在处理用户输入时，未经过滤的输入可能引发shell注入风险。文章提醒开发者在编写脚本和工具时需谨慎处理命令和参数，进行适当的转义和引用，以避免潜在的安全漏洞。尽管这个问题在多个操作系统的工具中普遍存在，但相关文档如POSIX手册中并未充分强调这一风险，因此开发者需格外注意。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于`system()`函数及其安全性问题的不同观点和讨论

不同观点：
• panzi观点：认为`system()`应该被废弃，特别是在新程序中不应使用。原因在于不同操作系统（如POSIX和Windows）对命令行解析的不一致性，尤其是在Windows中，每个程序可能有不同的解析方式。Rust对相关问题有明确警告，但Java等其他语言则没有。

• o11c观点：反对完全弃用`system()`，认为在某些情况下将命令传递给shell是必要的功能，例如`popen("gzip > foo.gz")`。任何涉及用户输入的情况都应事先进行 sanitize。批评文章中对`ssh`的指责，认为其作为shell命令执行工具并无不妥。

• GuB-42观点：`system()`有其存在的意义，适用于需要shell功能如管道的情况，类似于POSIX世界中的`eval()`。在安全性方面，若使用`system()`处理用户输入，相当于给予用户shell权限，需谨慎使用，或选择`exec*()`等替代方法。

• chubot观点：强调`printf '%q '`等工具在命令行参数引用中的重要性，并指出shell对参数的错误处理（如`ssh`的隐式`argv`连接）是安全问题的根源。提出shell设计缺陷，并建议Oils shell引入新的`invoke`内建命令来解决此问题。

• endiangroup观点：分享其在处理`ssh`命令限制工具中的经验，指出虽然其工具依赖于shell执行命令，但通过限制命令参数传递来缓解安全问题。

• pabs3观点：提到命令行选项允许代码执行的问题，并引用相关资料进行说明。

• Wicher观点：为解决`ssh`命令参数传递问题，提供了一个自制的pseudoshell工具，以便更安全地传递参数向量。

• ptx观点：认为shell命令执行问题并非Linux特有，而是UNIX体系的普遍问题。引用FreeBSD文档中的安全考虑说明。

• a_t48观点：推荐使用Python的`shlex.quote`来处理命令行参数引用问题，但强调最好的解决方案是尽可能避免使用shell命令。

• 1vuio0pswjnm7观点：讨论了不同shell（如bash和dash）的使用场景和性能差异，提出使用轻量级shell（如Almquist shell）的优点。

• 0xbadcafebee观点：认为文章讨论的问题是学习*NIX系统和shell脚本的常见困难，属于学习曲线的一部分，建议加强相关教育。

• blueflow观点：指出文章中对"command"和"argument vector"的混淆，认为这是导致误解的原因。

• zahlman观点：通过实验说明Python中调用shell命令与直接使用shell的不同表现，并提出如何处理特殊命令名称（如`-x`）的问题。

补充讨论：
• hackernudes观点：认为文章难以 follow，但同意`${var@Q}`和`printf '%q'`是有效的解决方案，希望能看到更多明显的引用方式以简化嵌套shell调用的处理。

44236241.article_content:
Some context
(For those interested only in the
glibc
and POSIX issues, see
at the end
.)
I use Linux almost everywhere, from laptops and desktops to servers and routers, and over the course of many years I've written quite a few
bash
scripts that ease my interaction with all of these.
The usual "stack" that ties all of these together is composed of:
bash
, obviously for scripting;
ssh
, for remote execution;
i3
, the window manager for desktop environments;
screen
, for terminal multiplexing;
tmux
, for terminal multiplexing;
dtach
, for launching processes in background while still being able to access them if needed;
(among many other tools like
coreutils
and friends,
grep
,
sed
,
sort
,
find
,
xargs
,
rsync
, plus other smaller C, Go or Rust based tools; but all of these are not the subject of this article;)
What do all of the former have in common? They all provide some sort of functionality, but by themselves they don't actually do anything; they are meant to delegate the actual work to other tools.
So what is the problem you ask? Nothing really... Everything is fine... No planes are falling from the sky... Nobody is running around screaming while on fire...
Everything is business as usual,
unless you want to write some wrapper scripts that takes arbitrary user input and delegates that to one of these, and many other, broken tools
...
And just for completeness I'll throw in some other tools that fit the bill:
make
(and any other variant or derivate), for build systems;
ninja
, my favorite build system, and lightweight DAG job scheduler and executer;
Root of all evil
As many of you have guessed, because we live in a UNIX world, many of these tools delegate the actual tool execution to the
glibc
system(3)
function,
which ends-up calling
sh(1p)
(most likely
bash
) with the
-c
argument.
As opposed to doing the correct thing and just calling
execve(2)
...
BTW, this is not something Linux specific. Unfortunately it is a trait inherited from the UNIX ancestry by almost all operating systems, including all BSD variants plus OSX;
and, for some tools, this behavior is even seen when running on Windows.
But I digress...
Excerpts from Linux
system(3)
man page
Let's quote from the Linux
system(3)
man page:
The
system(3)
library function uses
fork(2)
to create a child
process that executes the shell command specified in command
using
execl(3)
as follows:
execl("/bin/sh", "sh", "-c", command, (char *) NULL);
[...]
Any user input that is employed as part of command should be
carefully sanitized, to ensure that unexpected shell commands or
command options are not executed. Such risks are especially
grave when using
system()
from a privileged program.
So far the warning doesn't sound very comforting...
But hey, we are all responsible developers...
Excerpts from POSIX
system(3p)
man page
Let's quote from the POSIX
system(3p)
man page:
Hmm... Strange... There is nothing to quote from this manual about warnings, issues or sanitization...
(Except perhaps the warning for set-UID or set-GID processes against using this function, due to potential privilege escalation issues.)
Excerpts from POSIX
sh(1p)
man page
How about quoting from the POSIX
sh(1p)
man page regarding the
-c
flag:
-c
-- Read commands from the command_string operand. Set the
value of special parameter 0 (see Section 2.5.2,
Special Parameters) from the value of the command_name
operand and the positional parameters (
$1
,
$2
, and so
on) in sequence from the remaining argument operands.
No commands shall be read from the standard input.
OK... Still nothing about warnings, issues or sanitization...
Excerpts from
bash(1)
man page
Perhaps we'll have more luck quoting from the
bash(1)
man page:
-c
-- If the
-c
option is present, then commands are read from
the first non-option argument command_string. If there
are arguments after the
command_string
, the first argument
is assigned to
$0
and any remaining arguments are assigned
to the positional parameters. The assignment to
$0
sets
the name of the shell, which is used in warning and error
messages.
Hmm... Perhaps sanitization isn't that a big of an issue?
Partial conclusion
For now let's remember that initial remark:
Any user input [...] part of command should be [...] sanitized [...].
Aside from that, perhaps this "shell command" business I'm crying about isn't such a big of an issue?
Else the POSIX manuals for
system(3p)
(~2K words) and
sh(1p)
(~8K words)
-- that I assume were written by legions of committee members -- would have certainly spared at least a few words about this issue...
Right?
Unintended consequences
So why do we care about
system(3)
and
sh -c
?
Because as said in the beginning, many tools accept as arguments commands which in the end are passed to
sh -c
via the
system(3)
function.
Therefore when we write our scripts and tools we need to be aware of this situation and be prepared to escape and quote our commands and arguments accordingly,
else we'll be subject to
shell injections
... (For more sc

data.article_summary: CppNorth是将于2025年7月20-23日在加拿大多伦多举办的C++会议。此次大会为期三天，汇集本地及外邀讲者，提供学习、交流和探索C++社区新动态的机会。讲者阵容强大，包括Scott Hanselman、Alex Dathskovsky和Kate Gregory等。JetBrains和Autodesk分别是视频和金牌赞助商。会议酒店为King Edward Hotel，现已开放购票和预订。同时招募志愿者，参与者可选择现场或组织工作。大会还提供特别优惠，预订Royal York Hotel可享受800美元折扣。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对CppNorth会议的评价和看法

不同观点：
• [kazinator] 认为会议的演讲主题缺乏吸引力，显得无聊。他们的评论带有批评意味，表示对演讲内容的失望。

• [BiraIgnacio] 对会议持积极态度，强调了会议的价值，包括从多伦多用户组的成功经验中汲取力量，提供学习、社交和了解C++社区最新动态的机会，暗示会议对参与者有实质性的帮助。

• [babuloseo] 关注会议的票价，对高达1500美元的票价表示震惊，尤其在加拿大本地居民如何负担这样的费用上提出质疑，暗示票价可能过高，对普通参与者来说不太实惠。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是会议的质量和价值。一方面，[kazinator]质疑演讲主题的吸引力；另一方面，[BiraIgnacio]则强调会议的学习和社交机会，肯定其价值。
• 票价问题也是讨论的重点，[babuloseo]对高票价的质疑反映出对会议可负担性的担忧，这可能影响部分潜在参与者的参会意愿。

• [kazinator] 认为会议的演讲主题缺乏吸引力，显得无聊。他们的评论带有批评意味，表示对演讲内容的失望。

• [BiraIgnacio] 对会议持积极态度，强调了会议的价值，包括从多伦多用户组的成功经验中汲取力量，提供学习、社交和了解C++社区最新动态的机会，暗示会议对参与者有实质性的帮助。

• [babuloseo] 关注会议的票价，对高达1500美元的票价表示震惊，尤其在加拿大本地居民如何负担这样的费用上提出质疑，暗示票价可能过高，对普通参与者来说不太实惠。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是会议的质量和价值。一方面，[kazinator]质疑演讲主题的吸引力；另一方面，[BiraIgnacio]则强调会议的学习和社交机会，肯定其价值。
• 票价问题也是讨论的重点，[babuloseo]对高票价的质疑反映出对会议可负担性的担忧，这可能影响部分潜在参与者的参会意愿。

• **支持Git取代旧系统的观点**：[2d8a875f-39a2-4]指出，虽然Perforce和Source Depot在集中式版本控制系统时代表现出色，但技术已经发展，Git通过VFS解决了大仓库管理的问题，适应了现代需求。

44253212.article_content:
Part 7: Office Migration from Source Depot to Git, or how I learned to love DevEx.
June 10, 2025 · 11 minute read
Categories:
career
leadership
Tags:
technical
onenote
Series:
My career so far
After going in deep in product, I found myself drawn to a different challenge:
making other developers more productive
. As one of my biggest mentors would always say:
“Developer productivity is always ‘Multiplier work’, especially in places where you have a lot of developers. By saving a couple minutes from every developer, every day, you’ve saved years of human life waiting for stuff.”
The project that really forged me was the
Office migration from Source Depot to Git
.
Source Depot: A Journey to the Past
Come kids, gather around. Let me tell you youngsters about the ancient times of source control, back when dinosaurs roamed the Earth and before Git and GitHub were even a twinkle in Linus Torvalds’ eye.
In the early 2000s, Microsoft faced a dilemma. Windows was growing enormously complex, with millions of lines of code that needed versioning. Git? Didn’t exist. SVN? Barely crawling out of CVS’s shadow. No, children, these were the
dark ages
of version control.
Perforce was one of the few commercial options available—expensive but powerful for its time. Microsoft, being Microsoft, decided to build their own system based on Perforce technology. And thus,
Source Depot was born.
Using Source Depot was weird, it felt a little bit like
programming with oven mitts on
: iterations were faster, but branching and switching state were painful. Also, it didn’t help that a single get of the office repo took some hours. Want to check out code? Type
sd get (a.k.a osync)
and wait. And wait.
And perhaps make yourself a sandwich while waiting.
Branching? Oh, my sweet summer children. Creating a branch wasn’t the casual
git checkout -b
you casually toss around today. It was an
event
. Something you
planned
for, scheduled, and possibly created a small ritual around. (And pray you don’t have a name conflict.)
Everything was centralized—if the network went down,
productivity ceased
. If you were working remotely? Well,
VPN and prayer
were your only options. (And VPN was only to get into the AAD network and join the REDMOND domain.)
The worst part? Merging changes (or how we, the ancients, call them
Reverse Integrate
and
Forward Integrate
). Branch admins would constantly work on doing this process. You’d be
respected
by being the RI and FI admin for your part of your world.
Despite all this, Source Depot served Microsoft for many years. It was reliable, if nothing else, a sturdy workhorse. But by the time I encountered it, this workhorse was clearly showing its age.
This, my children, is why when we finally moved to Git, it took me, plus
some hundreds of engineers
,
years
to finalize.
Most challenging of all, Source Depot was deeply integrated into Microsoft’s build systems, release pipelines, and developer workflows. It wasn’t just source control, it was the foundation for how software was built at Microsoft.
Migrating OneNote to Git
At some point, the central developer experience organization (Office Engineering) decided that a migration to Git was needed. Not only was Source Depot a huge money sink, but patching it and maintaining it was a marathon job. They also had the grumbling of existing employees and new hires about not getting “
transferable job skills
”. This is how Office started their multi-year journey to migrate to Git.
This required
years of planning
. One day, I’ll gather the warriors who led this odyssey and ask them in detail their war stories over coffee. But from my tiny perspective, the challenges were the following:
Office has different schedules for different customers
LTSC (which ships in a > 6 months schedule, it’s
very stable
)
Semi-annual updates
Monthly updates
Insiders
Example of Office versions and naming schemes today
Which meant that any migration had to support the old and new system for months. Not only that, but Office versioning had to stay consistent between builds (which looked something like this 16.0.18730.20186, the latter part being the build number). This included triggering all the correct validation that happened in the previous system, keeping tests working (migrating the legacy test infra that only works on IE) and more.
The scale of Office
Today, as I type these words, I work at Snowflake. Snowflake has around
~2,000 engineers
. When I was in Office, Office alone was around
~4,000 engineers
. This required enormous coordination of the Office Engineering system with teams all around Office (
Word, Excel, Powerpoint, Sway, Publisher, Access, Project, OneNote, Shared Services (OSI), Shared UX, + everything in the we
b). Given these constraints, Office Engineering (OENG) created a “champion”/hub-spoke model. By designating one “Developer Satisfaction” champion per team, they would have an effective liaison per-team to not only migrate to Git, but to be able to have feedback channels for their

data.title: Introducing stronger dependencies on systemd
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: GNOME将加强对systemd的依赖，尤其是在GDM和gnome-session中。目前，GNOME的某些功能在没有systemd的环境下仍可运行，但未来更新将使这些功能更依赖systemd，增加非systemd发行版的运行难度。具体变化包括：GDM将依赖systemd的userdb来动态分配用户账户，取代现有hack方法，并计划移除AccountsService守护进程。此外，gnome-session将完全依赖systemd管理用户会话服务，移除老旧的内置服务管理器。对于没有systemd的发行版，需要自行实现systemd组件的替代品，如使用elogind等，以保持GNOME的兼容性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GNOME 对 systemd 的依赖及其影响

不同观点：
• [pona-a] 认为 systemd 由于其复杂性和紧密耦合的组件，成为了难以审核的系统，并且其功能增加了新的攻击面。此外，systemd 形成了垄断，排除了其他竞争性设计，导致系统难以替换。
• [surajrmal] 提出 systemd 提供的 API 应该独立出来，以便让更多外部开发者参与和实现这些 API，从而减少对 systemd 本身的严格依赖。
• [haileys] 支持 systemd，认为它是现代 Linux 基础设施的重要组成部分，相比以前的脚本化系统更加可靠和易用。
• [sph] 认为反对 systemd 的观点多是关于其"臃肿"和个人对开发者的偏见，而 systemd 已经成为桌面和服务器的主流选择，反对声音只是少数。
• [sunshine-o] 认为 GNOME 和桌面环境的变化对大多数用户影响不大，因为浏览器已经成为主要的用户界面，而高级用户会选择其他窗口管理器如 i3、sway 等。
• [cristodcgomez] 担心 GNOME 会逐渐演变成一个面向大众的 "Gnome OS"，并暗示这种情况可能已经不可避免。
• [n3storm] 推荐使用 Xfce 桌面环境，因其轻量、可定制，并且没有对 systemd 的依赖。
• [jabiko] 认为 GNOME 专注于单一代码路径是合理的，同时为非 systemd 系统提供指导，并将非 systemd 支持的责任转移给对此感兴趣的项目和用户。
• [noisy_boy] 讽刺地建议直接将 GNOME 改名为 "systemd-desktop"，表达对 GNOME 依赖 systemd 的不满。
• [petepete] 支持 GNOME 的决定，认为保持代码库的小型化和专注是合理的，尽管对非 Linux 用户可能带来痛苦。
• [hnlmorg] 对 GNOME 目前的市场份额表示疑问，认为自 GNOME 3 发布以来，其受欢迎程度没有明显回升。
• [bjourne] 指出在自由软件中添加多个后端支持往往导致高昂的维护成本，支持 systemd 避免了这种多后端问题，认为这是明智的设计决策。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于 systemd 的依赖性和其复杂性对系统安全性和可维护性的影响。
- 对 GNOME 依赖 systemd 是否会导致垄断和单一化的担忧。
- 对非 systemd 用户的支持和如何平衡开发资源的讨论。
- 对 GNOME 桌面环境在现代计算环境中的实际影响和市场份额的质疑。

44244646.article_content:
Introducing stronger dependencies on systemd
Jun 10, 2025
—
by
Adrian
in
systemd
Doesn’t GNOME already depend on systemd?
Kinda… GNOME doesn’t have a formal and well defined policy in place about systemd. The rule of thumb is that GNOME doesn’t strictly depend on systemd for critical desktop functionality, but individual features may break without it.
GNOME
does
strongly depend on logind, systemd’s session and seat management service. GNOME
first introduced support for logind in 2011
, then in 2015
ConsoleKit support was removed
and logind became a requirement. However, logind can exist in isolation from systemd: the modern
elogind
service does just that, and even back in 2015 there were
alternatives available
. Some distributors chose to
patch ConsoleKit support back into GNOME
. This way, GNOME can run in environments without systemd, including the BSDs.
While GNOME can run with other init systems, most upstream GNOME developers are not testing GNOME in these situations. Our automated testing infrastructure (i.e. GNOME OS) doesn’t test any non-systemd codepaths. And many modules that have non-systemd codepaths do so with the expectation that someone else will maintain them and fix them when they break.
What’s changing?
GNOME is about to gain a few strong dependencies on systemd, and this will make running GNOME harder in environments that don’t have systemd available.
Let’s start with the easier of the changes. GDM is
gaining a dependency
on systemd’s userdb infrastructure. GNOME and systemd do not support running more than one graphical session under the same user account, but GDM supports multi-seat configurations and
Remote Login with RDP
. This means that GDM may try to display multiple login screens at once, and thus multiple graphical sessions at once. At the moment, GDM relies on legacy behaviors and straight-up hacks to get this working, but this solution is
incompatible with the modern dbus-broker
and so we’re looking to clean this up. To that end, GDM now leverages systemd-userdb to dynamically allocate user accounts, and then runs each login screen as a unique user.
In the future, we plan to further depend on userdb by dropping the AccountsService daemon, which was designed to be a stop-gap measure for the lack of a rich user database. 15 years later, this “temporary” solution is still in use. Now that systemd’s userdb enables
rich user records
, we can start work on replacing AccountsService.
Next, the bigger change. Since GNOME 3.34, gnome-session uses the systemd user instance to start and manage the various GNOME session services. When systemd is unavailable, gnome-session falls back to a builtin service manager. This builtin service manager uses
.desktop
files to start up the various GNOME session services, and then monitors them for failure. This code was initially implemented for GNOME 2.24, and is starting to show its age. It has received very minimal attention in the 17 years since it was first written. Really, there’s no reason to keep maintaining a bespoke and somewhat primitive service manager when we have systemd at our disposal. The only reason this code hasn’t completely bit rotted is the fact that GDM’s aforementioned hacks break systemd and so we rely on the builtin service manager to launch the login screen.
Well, that has now changed. The hacks in GDM are gone, and the login screen’s session is managed by systemd. This means that the builtin service manager will now be completely unused and untested. Moreover: we’d like to implement a
session save/restore feature
, but the builtin service manager interferes with that. For this reason, the code
is being removed
.
So what should distros without systemd do?
First, consider using GNOME with systemd. You’d be running in a configuration supported, endorsed, and understood by upstream. Failing that, though, you’ll need to implement replacements for more systemd components, similarly to what you have done with elogind and eudev.
To help you out, I’ve put a temporary alternate code path into GDM that makes it possible to run GDM without an implementation of userdb. When compiled against elogind, instead of trying to allocate dynamic users GDM will look-up and use the
gdm-greeter
user for the first login screen it spawns,
gdm-greeter-2
for the second, and
gdm-greeter-N
for the Nth. GDM will have similar behavior with the
gnome-initial-setup[-N]
users. You can statically allocate as many of these users as necessary, and GDM will work with them for now. It’s quite likely that this will be necessary for GNOME 49.
Next: you’ll need to deal with the removal of gnome-session’s builtin service manager. If you don’t have a service manager running in the user session, you’ll need to get one. Just like system services, GNOME session services now install systemd unit files, and you’ll have to replace these unit files with your own service manager’s definitions. Next, you’ll need to replace the “session leader” process: this is the main gnome-sess

data.title: The hunt for Marie Curie's radioactive fingerprints in Paris
data.author: rmason
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了记者苏菲·哈达克前往巴黎玛丽·居里生前工作的实验室，使用盖革计数器追踪她遗留的放射性指纹。居里夫人在20世纪初进行放射性研究时，常裸手接触放射性物质，导致她的物品和笔记上留下了微量放射性痕迹。这些痕迹在实验室的门把手、椅子以及她的书籍和笔记上被发现，放射性水平低且对人体无害。一些受污染严重的物品，如一个柜子，已被作为核废料处理。居里夫人的女儿伊雷娜也可能留下了部分痕迹。专家马克·阿莫里希负责检测这些物品，他认为追踪这些痕迹不仅是保存历史遗产，也让人联想到当时的科研环境和工作方式。

补充讨论：
• [shmeano] 提出是否可以制造放射性摄像机的问题，引发对放射性技术可行性和物理特性的讨论。尽管这是一个技术性问题，但与主题相关，显示出对放射性现象的进一步好奇和探讨。

争议焦点：
• 居里夫人名字的正确使用成为一个小争议点，[odiroot] 对媒体简化其名字的做法提出批评，强调对历史和个人身份的尊重。

44231386.article_content:
The hunt for Marie Curie's radioactive fingerprints in Paris
3 days ago
Share
Save
Sophie Hardach
Share
Save
Edouard Taufenbach and Bastien Pourtout
(Credit: Edouard Taufenbach and Bastien Pourtout)
Marie Curie worked with radioactive material with her bare hands. More than 100 years after her groundbreaking work, Sophie Hardach travels to Paris to trace the lingering radioactive fingerprints she left behind.
The Geiger counter starts flashing and buzzing as I hold it against the 100-year-old Parisian doorknob. I am standing in the doorway between the historical lab and office of Marie Curie, the Polish-born, Paris-based scientist who invented the word "radioactivity" – and here is an especially startling trace of her. The museum that houses the lab has invited me in here to track radioactive handprints left by her when she worked here in the early 20th Century. Here, on the doorknob, is one such trace. There's another one on the back of her chair. Many more of these invisible traces are dotted all over her archived notes, books and private furniture, some only discovered in recent years.
The Geiger counter's reaction, and the numbers on the display, suggest the presence of above-background radioactivity, though only at low and non-threatening levels. In
microsievert
, which measures the potential impact of radiation on the human body, it comes to about 0.24 microsievert per hour, well within safe
limits
, according to experts.
Marie Curie worked here from
1914 until 1934
, the year of her death, handling radioactive elements including radium, which she and her husband Pierre Curie had discovered in 1898. For most of her life, she did this with bare, increasingly radium-
scarred
hands. She then transferred traces of these elements onto other things she touched. Tracking the handprints through her work spaces, one can imagine how she might have gone "from the lab to the office, opened the door and pulled out the office chair to sit down", says Renaud Huynh, the director of the Curie Museum, as he guides me from trace to trace.
Edouard Taufenbach and Bastien Pourtout
The faintly radioactive doorknob at the Curie Museum (Credit: Edouard Taufenbach and Bastien Pourtout)
Some radioactive traces, for example in the Curies' lab notes and
notebooks
, have long been known about: one analysis in the 1950s made some of them
visible
by using a photographic plate. The contamination showed up as dots and splodges, suggesting
radioactive lab dust
settling on the page, or droplets from boiling solutions of
radium salts
spraying onto it.
Other traces have been revealed in more depth by further
tests
in recent years: they have been found on the doors of a
cupboard
from her home, on drawers, on the pages of books, on lecturing notes, and even on an extendable dining table from the Curies' family home.
For every item, experts face the agonising question of whether to save it as heritage – or, in cases where the contamination is considered a public safety risk, put into a nuclear waste facility. The cupboard, for example, ended up being destroyed.
Getty Images
Marie Curie handled radioactive substances for much of her career with bare hands (Credit: Getty Images)
Marie Curie's lab and office, whose tall windows overlook a rose garden she designed, are usually closed off by a red cordon, to be viewed but not entered by the museum's visitors. They were part of the
Radium Institute
, which she founded, and still sit in the heart of an active, bustling research
campus
.
"There's a great probability that the radioactive traces were left by Marie Curie, but it could have been her
daughter
[Irène Joliot-Curie], who later used the same office," says Huynh. "Either way, it's a material trace of the past, it's a form of heritage. If we were to erase these traces, we would lose this memory. It might be a detail, but it evokes a mode of contamination, it evokes a certain way of working – and it also evokes an era."
It's like holding the history of radioactivity in my hands – Marc Ammerich
Huynh has invited me into the museum outside opening hours, and also into the nearby archive, to talk about these traces. Since radioactivity is invisible, I had asked him before the visit if I could bring a Geiger counter to bring the traces to life for our readers. He agreed, and also let me invite Marc Ammerich, a radiation expert, to help me measure and interpret the results.
Ammerich spent 40 years working for French radioprotection agencies, inspecting the safety of France's nuclear power plants. Since 2019, he has been tasked with
comprehensive tests
on the museum's collection. He has tested about 9,000 items from the Curies and their family so far, including the extendable dining table, where he found two radioactive patches next to each other, like two handprints, where a person would grab the table and pull it out for visitors.

data.title: AOSP project is coming to an end
data.author: kaladin-jasnah
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google是否会终止Android Open Source Project (AOSP) 以及该项目对不同设备制造商和开发者的影响。

不同观点：
• **AOSP不会被终止**：[xnx]引用了Google的声明，明确表示AOSP不会被终止，强调AOSP作为一个开放平台的持续重要性，并且Cuttlefish和GSI目标仍然可用于测试和开发。
• **Pixel设备的支持问题**：[transpute]担心Pixel设备对AOSP的支持可能会延迟或终止，特别是考虑到Pixel设备在运行Debian Linux和桌面模式方面的独特优势。[sebtron]也提到这可能仅影响Google Pixel设备，并询问对其他制造商如Fairphone的影响。
• **Pixel设备锁定**：[prmoustache]认为更准确的说法是Google正在锁定Pixel平台，而不是终止AOSP。[pzo]表达了对Pixel设备不再支持clean Android的失望，并询问其他支持自定义ROM的设备。
• **未来可能的变化**：[SlowTao]预测AOSP的终止可能在未来五年内发生，但未提供具体时间框架。[nickburns]提供了一个更谨慎的观点链接，提到Google可能有意对AOSP做出改变。[bubblethink]质疑Google在Android领域已经取得主导地位后为何要做出这样的改变，并提到Google Play服务的限制。

补充讨论：
• **开发工具和SDK**：[palata]提出了如果Google将AOSP专有化，会对Android SDK和开发者工具产生什么影响的问题，指出Android SDK并非开源。[xbmcuser]猜测Google可能在等待新Pixel硬件发布后再发布AOSP更新。
• **Play商店的使用**：[DidYaWipe]询问是否可以在AOSP上使用Play商店，并对Google的操作表示怀疑。[skeledrew]提到Android Market变为Google Play Store后，AOSP的功能逐渐被迁移到GMS，认为这预示着未来可能的改变。
• **设备树的更新**：[petabyt]询问Pixel设备树为何需要在不同Android版本中更新，并推测这些差异可能较小。

争议的焦点：
• AOSP是否会被终止或变得更为专有，以及这对开发者和设备制造商的具体影响。
• Google Pixel设备对AOSP的支持变化及其对用户选择的影响。

这些观点反映了社区对Google在Android项目上未来策略的关注和不确定性。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[机械设备的标准化描述及具体应用]

不同观点：
• [downboots] 提出是否存在一种标准化的方式来描述机械设备，类似于用 .obj 文件定义3D形状。他希望这种标准能够描述零件类型、交互、属性、运动范围等，并希望计算机能够利用这种格式从类似 https://507movements.com/ 的目录中找到有趣的配置，结合模拟（如迪士尼研究项目中齿轮和连杆的模拟）来实现。

• [burnt-resistor] 对望远镜式吊臂内部结构感兴趣，尤其是多节结构可以相互嵌套。他提到澳大利亚的 CEE 频道正在修复一台 Frena 起重机，通过禁用一些不必要的部分来简化操作，尽管这样做会牺牲一些负载能力和稳定性。

• [EricRiese] 提出了一个创意，希望能看到有人用这种机制制作一个"复合长号"（compound trombone）。

• [edweis] 则关注这些机械结构是否在工业层面得到应用，提出了对该技术实际工业用途的疑问。

补充讨论：
• [downboots] 关注的是机械设备描述的标准化和计算机辅助设计与模拟的可能性，强调了标准化格式对机械设计自动化的重要性。

• [burnt-resistor] 通过具体实例（望远镜式吊臂）展示了多节结构的实际应用和其在特定情况下的实用性。

• [EricRiese] 从一个创意角度出发，提出了将机械结构应用到乐器设计中的可能性。

• [edweis] 则更关注这些技术的实际工业应用，反映了讨论从理论和创意到实际应用的延展。

争议焦点：
• 目前没有明确的争议，但不同参与者关注的角度不同，有的关注理论和标准化，有的关注实际应用，还有的从创意角度出发。这反映了讨论在理论与实际应用之间的张力。

本文介绍了如何在Ruby中用30分钟构建一个简易的装饰器模式。作者由于项目中的Rails版本较旧，无法使用Draper gem，于是决定手动构建一个装饰器。文章首先展示了`Teacher`类的基本结构及其与`Student`类的关系，随后解释了在视图中展示教师可用位置并根据数量显示不同背景色的需求。

作者指出，不应在模型中编写生成CSS类的方法，而应使用装饰器。接着，文章展示了如何创建一个简单的`TeacherDecorator`，并通过`method_missing`方法将未定义的方法调用转发给原始的`Teacher`对象，从而使装饰器能够处理自身的公共方法以及被装饰对象的公共方法。最终，实现了装饰器与模型方法的兼容，确保视图中可以正常调用`Teacher`的方法。

总结：本文通过构建一个简易的装饰器，展示了如何在不修改模型的情况下，在视图中添加与显示相关的逻辑，并利用Ruby的`method_missing`方法实现方法转发。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rails中使用视图助手（view helpers）与装饰器（decorators）的优劣对比，以及对设计模式的正确使用和Ruby语言性能问题的讨论。

不同观点：
• **pmontra**：支持使用Rails自带的视图助手方法，如`colour_coded_availability(teacher)`，认为这样无需元编程、装饰器或引入新概念，符合标准Rails实践，并且是一种函数式编程的实例。
• **estsauver**：担心这种做法可能会影响Ruby虚拟机的虚拟方法缓存，引发性能问题，尤其是动态方法路由或类扩展可能导致痛苦的经验。
• **berkes**：批评Ruby社区对设计模式的滥用和不准确的使用，尤其是“装饰器”。认为Ruby中的“装饰器”（如Draper）引入了新的方法，违背了Liskov替换原则（LSP）和依赖倒置原则（DIP），并且在视图和控制器之间引入了不必要的依赖，可能导致生产环境中的崩溃问题。
• **firecall**：个人经验认为使用Draper装饰器在旧项目中带来了不便，视图逻辑被隐藏，不易维护。
• **inopinatus**：建议先花时间探索和学习，然后使用标准库中的`SimpleDelegator`实现装饰器功能，且态度较为中立。
• **sirk390**：提出更简单的条件判断方式，直接在视图中使用三元运算符，避免复杂性。
• **byroot**：指出从Ruby 3.0开始，`method_missing`的签名不正确，需要处理关键字参数，并给出正确写法。
• **ht85**：对使用复杂代码表示质疑，甚至将其与Perl的一次性正则表达式相比较，隐含对代码可读性的担忧。
• **sathishmanohar**：质疑讨论中混淆了装饰器模式（如AvailableTeacher或UnavailableTeacher）和视图助手的角色，认为这是两个不同的概念。
• **lmz**：引用其他讨论中的相关评论，暗示可能有更多相关的讨论。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于装饰器与视图助手之间的选择，以及Ruby社区对设计模式术语的不准确使用。
- 性能问题也是讨论中的一个重要方面，尤其是与Ruby虚拟机和动态方法相关的性能影响。
- 对装饰器模式的误用和视图逻辑的处理是另一个值得注意的讨论点。

44254984.article_content: Build a minimal decorator with Ruby in 30 minutes ← Return to the Ruby blog A few weeks ago, I needed to add some view-related methods to an object. Decorators are my go-to pattern to handle this kind of logic. Normally, I’d use the draper gem to build decorators. But the app I’m working on used an older and incompatible version of Rails. So I built a minimal decorator from scratch, added a bunch of extra behaviors, only to end up abstracting all of these away. Follow along! What I’m working with My Teacher class has a handful of methods: A one-to-many relationship with the Student class. Two public methods: one that exposes the maximum number of students a teacher can teach to, and one exposing the available teaching places. class Teacher < ApplicationRecord has_many :students def maximum_number_of_students = 30 def available_places ( maximum_number_of_students <=> students . size ). clamp ( 0 .. ) end end In my views, I want to display a table of teachers where the number of available places for each teacher is backed by a background colour. # teachers/index.html.erb < table class = "table table-striped" > < thead > < tr > < th > Name of the teacher < /th> Available places < /tr> < tbody > < % teachers.each do | teacher | %> < td >< %= teacher.full_name %> < %= teacher.available_places %> <% end %> I could write the Teacher#colour_coded_availability method in my model like so: class Teacher < ApplicationRecord has_many :students def maximum_number_of_students = 30 def available_places ( maximum_number_of_students <=> students . size ). clamp ( 0 .. ) end def colour_coded_availability case available_places when 0 then "bg-colour-red" else "bg-colour-green" end end end However, models are not the place for methods generating CSS classes. Decorators are! Drafting a decorator My decorator should accept an instance of Teacher and expose the colour_coded_availability public method. # app/decorators/teacher_decorator.rb class TeacherDecorator attr_reader :teacher def initialize ( teacher :) @teacher = teacher end def colour_coded_availability case teacher . available_places when 0 then "bg-colour-red" else "bg-colour-green" end end end Now, I can instantiate my decorator and use it in my views: # app/controllers/teachers_controller.rb class TeachersController < ApplicationController def index @teachers = Teacher . all . map { TeacherDecorator . new ( teacher: _1 ) } end end # teachers/index.html.erb < table class = "table table-striped" > < thead > < tr > < th > Name of the teacher < /th> Available places < /tr> < tbody > < % @teachers.each do | teacher | %> < td >< %= teacher.full_name %> < %= teacher.available_places %> <% end %> When I can call teacher.colour_coded_availability in my views, the method retrieves a CSS class and adds it to the HTML tag. But if I were to run this code as is, I’d get a beautiful NoMethodError . Why? My views do not handle instances of Teacher anymore. They handle instances of TeacherDecorator . So, when I’m calling the public methods defined on Teacher , the decorator doesn’t know what to do with them. My decorator needs to be able to handle both its own public methods and the public methods defined on the underlying record ( Teacher , in this case). And we do that by using Ruby’s method_missing . Ruby’s method_missing to the rescue method_missing is how Ruby handles method calls made on objects where said methods are not defined. Ruby passes the method call along the ancestry chain until it can either resolves it or raises a NoMethodError . When I call @teacher.full_name , I want my decorator to rescue the NoMethodError , and forward #full_name to the underlying instance of Teacher . To do that, I need to re-open Ruby’s method_missing , add a custom behavior, then allow method_missing to run its normal course. class TeacherDecorator attr_reader :teacher def initialize ( teacher ) @teacher = teacher end def availability_as_background case teacher . max_number_of_students <=> teacher . available_places when - 1 then "background-danger" when 0 then "background-warning" when 1 then "background-success" end end private def method_missing ( method , * args , & ) return teacher . public_send ( method , * args , & ) if teacher . respond_to? ( method ) super end def respond_to_missing? ( name , include_private = false ) teacher . respond_to? ( name ) || super end end In this example, I keep the original signature of Ruby’s method_missing . The only thing I tweak is forwarding the method call to the underlying teacher . I only forward it if the teacher responds to the method. Then, I let Ruby resume its original behavior 1 . Now, @teacher.full_name is properly forwarded to the underlying instance of Teacher . data.title: How much EU is in DNS4EU?
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了DNS4EU项目的实际"欧洲化"程度。DNS4EU是由欧盟网络安全局支持的项目，旨在为欧盟提供安全、隐私合规的DNS服务。文章通过DNS查询、Whois和BGP等工具分析了该项目的域名服务器、网站托管和邮件服务。结果显示，尽管DNS服务器由欧盟公司运营，但其网站托管使用了美国公司Cloudflare的服务，邮件服务则依赖于Google。此外，路由分析显示部分流量通过非欧盟国家的ASN传输，尤其是英国（脱欧后不再属于欧盟）。因此，文章得出结论，DNS4EU项目虽然在某些方面符合"欧盟化"，但在关键服务和基础设施上仍依赖非欧盟公司，最终评分仅为1:3。文章还对项目的单点故障问题提出质疑，建议采用多 provider 的anycast方式提升可靠性和安全性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：欧洲是否拥有真正的自主网络服务（如DNS和云服务）以及DNS4EU项目的有效性和自主性。

不同观点：
• AndroTux认为，欧洲缺乏像Cloudflare和Google Workspace这样的自主服务，即使有一些部分替代方案，但企业很难投入资源去构建完全自主的替代品。
• supermatt指出，DNS4EU的营销网站与实际运营的基础设施不同，虽然使用了美国的基础设施，但这并不影响DNS4EU提供公共解析器的使命。
• benjojo12反驳了仅凭WHOIS信息判断服务是否为欧盟所有的做法，并表示愿意使用来自英国、瑞士等地的优质服务。
• lpcvoid分享了自己从Cloudflare迁移到deSEC.io的成功经验，认为deSEC.io是一个良好的欧盟替代方案。
• karel-3d担心DNS4EU未按要求在某些国家屏蔽特定内容，可能违反当地法律。
• rozumbrada解释了数据路由的复杂性，指出不能简单地通过WHOIS信息判断数据流向。
• _joel质疑DNS4EU的基础设施是否真正为欧盟服务，还是仅为设计公司所用。
• gbil提供了RIPE数据库中的ASN信息，指出DNS4EU的上游 peers包括匈牙利和英国的网络。
• tazjin认为DNS4EU未按要求屏蔽某些应被 censored 的网站，质疑其与政府的一致性。
• miyuru质疑公共解析器的必要性，认为网络运营者可以轻易设置自己的递归服务器。
• johncoltrane提醒注意英国已脱欧，因此.uk域名不应视为欧盟的一部分。
• ju-st通过dig命令查询发现joindns4.eu的域名服务器位于美国和英国。
• fside批评DNS4EU只是将查询集中到一个欧盟品牌的端点，并没有真正解决隐私和弹性问题。
• ExoticPearTree认为实现100%的欧盟自主服务不切实际，更多是政治幻想。
• jedisct1指出DNS4EU缺乏对现代隐私协议的支持，如ODoH和Anonymized DNSCrypt。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于DNS4EU是否真正实现了欧盟的网络自主，特别是在基础设施和隐私保护方面。
• 讨论中多次提到英国脱欧对服务归属的影响，以及如何有效判断服务是否真正自主。
• 对公共解析器的必要性和隐私保护的讨论，也反映出用户对服务质量和数据安全的关注。

通过这些观点，可以看到关于欧盟网络自主的讨论涉及技术、法律和政治多个层面，并且在实际操作中存在诸多挑战。

44255116.article_content:
How much EU is in DNS4EU?
2025-06-11
#
DNS
This is another post that started after several toots on mastodon. Most of the
things presented here were already tooted by other people, but I think this is
a good chance to write a mini tutorial about what to look at. We’ll use
DNS, whois, BGP and your favourite search engine.
What is DNS4EU?
#
To quote the web page:
Supported by the European Union Agency for Cybersecurity (ENISA),
the European Union’s DNS4EU secure-infrastructure project provides
a protective, privacy-compliant, and resilient DNS service to
strengthen digital sovereignty and security for EU citizens, governments,
and critical infrastructure.
First things first
#
The first thing your computer does is to do a DNS lookup, so let’s do the
same:
$ dig ns joindns4.eu +short
ns63.cloudns.net.
ns64.cloudns.uk.
ns61.cloudns.net.
Searching for clouddns you’ll find that they are  a European
company. Going one step further we can check the IPv4 and IPv6 addresses of
the three name servers above and see that all of them are from providers within
the EU.
$ for i in $(dig ns joindns4.eu +short); do host $i; done
ns61.cloudns.net has address 109.201.133.168
ns61.cloudns.net has IPv6 address 2a00:1768:1001:9::168
ns64.cloudns.uk has address 185.206.180.150
ns64.cloudns.uk has IPv6 address 2a0b:1640:1:1:1:1:15ee:539e
ns63.cloudns.net has address 51.210.104.220
ns63.cloudns.net has IPv6 address 2001:41d0:304:200::455b
You can check all of them yourself by using
whois
on the command line. I’m
leaving that out to keep this post short.
EU:NON-EU 1:0
www.joindns4.eu
So let’s look at the website:
$ host www.joindns4.eu
www.joindns4.eu is an alias for 142290803.sites.hscoscdn-eu1.net.
142290803.sites.hscoscdn-eu1.net has address 141.101.90.98
142290803.sites.hscoscdn-eu1.net has address 141.101.90.99
142290803.sites.hscoscdn-eu1.net has address 141.101.90.96
142290803.sites.hscoscdn-eu1.net has address 141.101.90.97
142290803.sites.hscoscdn-eu1.net has IPv6 address 2a06:98c1:3200::90:0
142290803.sites.hscoscdn-eu1.net has IPv6 address 2a06:98c1:3200::90:2
142290803.sites.hscoscdn-eu1.net has IPv6 address 2a06:98c1:3200::90:3
142290803.sites.hscoscdn-eu1.net has IPv6 address 2a06:98c1:3200::90:1
For IPv4 the RIPE database seems to need some cleanup, for IPv6 we
get:
$ whois 2a06:98c1:3200::90:0 | grep netname
netname:        CLOUDFLARENET-EU
Cloudflare is an American company. EU:NON-EU 1:1
What about mail?
#
Let’s look at the mail servers:
$ dig mx joindns4.eu +short
1 aspmx.l.google.com.
5 alt1.aspmx.l.google.com.
5 alt2.aspmx.l.google.com.
10 aspmx3.googlemail.com.
10 aspmx2.googlemail.com.
So they are using Google for mail, which again is an American company.
EU:NON-EU 1:2
It was pointed out to me that it’s called DNS4EU and not MAIL4EU or WEB4EU,
so feel free to ignore all this. Europeans can’t do web and mail. There is
absolutely no provider here who can do such complicated tasks.
But let’s look at their “product”
#
All the DNS resolvers that you can / should configure are in
2a13:1001::86:54:11:/64 and 86.54.11.100/24. Which are, according to whois,
registered by a company from the EU. So 2:2? Not so fast. We must go one step
further and look into BGP, the routing protocol used on the Internet.
There are several publicly accessible, read-only, BGP routers available to
ask, see the
route-views project
Many providers also offer a Looking glass so you can see the provider’s view
of the BGP world.
Note that I removed all but the relevant information so the output does not get
too confusing:
$ telnet route-views.amsix.routeviews.org
route-views.amsix.routeviews.org> sh bgp ipv6 2a13:1001::86:54:11
BGP routing table entry for 2a13:1001::/48, version 327804
Paths: (22 available, best #1, table default)
[...]
15943 60068 198121
[...]
51088 60068 198121
[...]
1103 60068 198121
[...]
12779 60068 198121
[...]
38880 6939 60068 198121
[...]
60150 5405 60068 198121
[...]
BGP uses AS numbers for routing and the above output shows us the way from
the Amsix route-views router to our destination in AS198121.
Once again we can use whois to query information about these ASN. You just
need to put AS in front of the number when asking.
There is way more output, try for yourself:
$ whois as198121 | grep country
country:        CZ
Ah, good - EU!  Not so fast… Note that the second to last AS is always the same.
$ whois as60068 | grep country
country:        GB
Last time I checked GB was not part of the EU. And it’s also a member of FIVE
eyes.
So we have a service sponsored by EU, to protect the privacy of EU citizens
using mainly non-EU services and routing all of their traffic, at least for
the sample I took, via an non-EU provider.
So final score, depending on how you count:
EU:NON-EU 1:3
And then there is the issue of being single homed. How do they achieve
availability / redundancy and avoid being DDOSed? I would expect such a service
to be anycasted, available via multiple providers (all EU-based). But that’s
just me doing free consul

• karel-3d担心DNS4EU未按要求在某些国家屏蔽特定内容，可能违反当地法律。
• rozumbrada解释了数据路由的复杂性，指出不能简单地通过WHOIS信息判断数据流向。
• _joel质疑DNS4EU的基础设施是否真正为欧盟服务，还是仅为设计公司所用。
• gbil提供了RIPE数据库中的ASN信息，指出DNS4EU的上游 peers包括匈牙利和英国的网络。
• tazjin认为DNS4EU未按要求屏蔽某些应被 censored 的网站，质疑其与政府的一致性。
• miyuru质疑公共解析器的必要性，认为网络运营者可以轻易设置自己的递归服务器。
• johncoltrane提醒注意英国已脱欧，因此.uk域名不应视为欧盟的一部分。
• ju-st通过dig命令查询发现joindns4.eu的域名服务器位于美国和英国。
• fside批评DNS4EU只是将查询集中到一个欧盟品牌的端点，并没有真正解决隐私和弹性问题。
• ExoticPearTree认为实现100%的欧盟自主服务不切实际，更多是政治幻想。
• jedisct1指出DNS4EU缺乏对现代隐私协议的支持，如ODoH和Anonymized DNSCrypt。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于DNS4EU是否真正实现了欧盟的网络自主，特别是在基础设施和隐私保护方面。
• 讨论中多次提到英国脱欧对服务归属的影响，以及如何有效判断服务是否真正自主。
• 对公共解析器的必要性和隐私保护的讨论，也反映出用户对服务质量和数据安全的关注。

通过这些观点，可以看到关于欧盟网络自主的讨论涉及技术、法律和政治多个层面，并且在实际操作中存在诸多挑战。

data.title: Danish Ministry Replaces Windows and Microsoft Office with Linux and LibreOffice
data.author: jlpcsl
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：丹麦政府部门计划从Microsoft Office和Windows迁移到LibreOffice和Linux，以及相关的基础设施和规划问题。

不同观点：
• mrweasel认为迁移不仅仅是更换Office和Windows，还包括整个周边基础设施的问题，例如认证、邮件系统和文件共享。他预测由于规划不足和培训缺乏，这次迁移将以失败告终。
• rcbdev提到奥地利司法部使用LibreOffice多年，并指出微软可能会通过游说来干预这种迁移。
• clejack认为政府在许可费用上花费过多，应该投资于开源软件，以减少对微软和谷歌等公司的依赖。
• gggggggoodlord指出，这次迁移仅涉及一个80人的部门，而不是更大的附属机构，因此影响有限。相比之下，哥本哈根和奥胡斯市的类似计划涉及80,000名员工，影响更大。
• ThinkBeat担心员工需要时间适应LibreOffice，这可能导致工作效率下降，并产生抵触情绪。
• reacharavindh提到丹麦的公司和政府机构深陷微软生态系统，但建议使用免费或开源的在线办公软件作为替代方案。
• mettamage主张政府应资助更多开源项目，但要避免过于强硬的推动导致项目半途而废。
• chuckadams认为整个迁移计划在不到6个月内完成是不现实的，可能只是与微软谈判的策略。
• piker指出微软在许多行业的垄断地位，并赞赏丹麦的迁移计划作为一种应对措施。
• Tangokat认为特朗普政府对美国服务的信任损害导致欧洲国家寻求脱离美国服务提供商，丹麦的迁移计划是这种趋势的一部分。
• bazoom42澄清说，这次迁移仅涉及用LibreOffice替换Microsoft Office 365，而不包括用Linux替换Windows。
• phkamp提到，这次迁移只影响约79名员工。
• henriquenunez对丹麦的迁移计划表示热烈支持。
• whiplash451预测丹麦可能会在3年后重新使用微软产品。
• trelane建议使用Collabora或其他类似服务，以获得支持并帮助开源软件的开发。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于迁移的可行性和规划的充分性。一些人认为丹麦政府没有充分准备和投资于培训及基础设施，这可能导致项目失败。
• 另一个讨论点是政治因素，特别是特朗普政府对美国服务信任的损害如何促使欧洲国家寻求替代方案。
• 还有对微软在行业垄断地位的担忧，以及开源软件在政府和企业中应用的潜力。
